summary.text: 洗 is a water-related phonosemantic character: 氵 marks the water category, while 先 is traditionally identified as its sound element. An early dictionary gloss associates it with washing the feet; current meanings include washing, rinsing, and cleaning.

formation.text: Phonosemantic. The traditional analysis assigns water meaning to 氵 and a phonetic role to 先. The phonetic identification is a historical account; sound comparisons are suggestive but do not independently prove the ancient relation.

components.text: 氵 is the conventional side form of 水. In this character it contributes the water category; it is not a separate picture of a washing scene.
先 is named in the traditional analysis as the sound element. A modern seal-script-style drawing illustrates 先, but is not an early form of 洗.

sound_limitation.text: The supplied readings permit a notation-specific comparison, but do not independently prove that this graphic element had the compared ancient pronunciation or establish its phonetic role. Current Mandarin readings are also not evidence of an ancient relation.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart 2014 table, 先 is MC sen and 洗 has a reading MC senX; their similar forms support a comparison in this system. The same table gives 先 OC *sˤər and 洗 OC *sˤərʔ. The dossier cautions that these entries alone do not prove the historical component relation.

history.text: The traditional account analyzes 洗 as 水 plus phonetic 先 and glosses it as washing the feet. A modern illustration in the curated selection depicts 先 in Shuowen seal-script style; it is not an early 洗 glyph. No verified historical image of 洗 or secure early graphic sequence is supplied.

A reported oracle-bone graph has been identified as 洗 by one scholar and as 歬 by another. A scholarly proposal connects early forms with foot washing and suggests that 歬 was later used to write ‘go forward’; the identification and proposed relationship remain unsettled, and the glyphs were not independently inspected.

Later accounts report overlap between 洗 and 洒: some treat 洒 as a variant or ancient form of 洗, while another says 洗 later replaced 洒 for general washing. This evidence does not establish 洒 as 洗’s original graphic form.

uncertainties.text: The dossier does not resolve the disputed identification of the oracle-bone graph or establish a secure early graphic sequence for 洗.

The sound comparison is notation-specific and does not independently establish the ancient pronunciation of the graphic component or prove its phonetic function; current Mandarin readings do not settle that question.

The cited transmitted texts document distinct uses, but exact manuscript dates, the first attested use, and a chronological path among foot washing, vessel-related uses, general washing, and purification are not established.

senses.text: An early lexicographic gloss associates 洗 with washing the feet; cited transmitted texts also document this use, without establishing the exact first occurrence.

The character is used with the meanings wash and rinse. The evidence also cites washing the head, feet, hands, and body, but does not establish a linear development from the foot-washing gloss to broader washing.
Clean and purify are recorded meanings. The dossier does not establish when or by what path these meanings developed.

senses.gloss: a vessel associated with wash water
senses.text: A cited ritual text uses 洗 for a vessel receiving wash water; this word-level use is separately recorded and its chronology relative to washing is unresolved.
A cited text uses 洗 for washing a ritual vessel. The evidence does not establish its precise date or relation in time to other washing uses.

limitations.text: Cited examples come from transmitted works and do not establish exact manuscript dates, a first attestation, or a linear semantic chronology among the recorded uses.

overview.text: 洗 combines the water marker 氵 with 先, traditionally identified as a sound element. It means ‘wash’ or ‘rinse’; an early dictionary gloss specifically associates it with washing the feet.

components.text: 氵 supplies the water category, helping place the character in the domain of washing.
先 is traditionally identified as the sound element; the historical sound link is not independently proved by the available comparison.

relationships.text: 氵, the side form of 水, contributes the water category in 洗.

The traditional analysis identifies 先 as the sound element. In the Baxter–Sagart 2014 table, 先 has MC sen and OC *sˤər, while 洗 has a listed reading MC senX and OC *sˤərʔ; this is a suggestive comparison, not independent proof of the ancient graphic relation.
